transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-16
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Shoreline VP Eng), Aisha Rahman (Shoreline ML Eng), Tom Rios (Shoreline CTO)

Summary (auto): Discovery for model selection and deployment mode; discussed long-context needs, multilingual eval, tool-calling and security. Next steps and owners captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — i'm samir from Redwood, with priya our solutions eng. how are we doing?
[00:12] Mark: doing well thanks. quick note, we're on pacific time but this works.
[00:18] Tom: hi all, tom here, i'll be mostly listening but i'll jump in on infra/security questions.
[00:24] Aisha: hey, aisha — i'll be driving the ML evals side. excited to dig in.
[00:30] Priya: awesome. goal today is to understand your model selection constraints — context length, multilingual, tool calling, and whether hosted/dedicated/private fits.
[00:42] Mark: high level — we're building a knowledge assistant for maritime analytics, needs to ingest and reason over long voyage logs. typical session could be 30k-50k tokens, sometimes up to 80k for batch. latency ideally <800ms for interactive parts but batch can be slower.
[01:05] Samir: ok that's helpful — so long-context is front-and-center. on the model side do you have a preference for closed vs open models? we often recommend curated open models for dedicated/private to control cost.
[01:22] Mark: prefer open for cost and auditability. we'd like to avoid closed APIs if possible.
[01:28] Aisha: also multilingual — english and spanish primary, with some japanese. must preserve domain-specific terminology.
[01:36] Priya: got it. for 50k+ contexts we typically look at long-context variants or models with efficient attention — we can bench Redwood's long-context configs. question: do you need function-calling to orchestrate tool calls to your retrieval system and DB?
[01:54] Mark: yes, we need tool-calling. the assistant should call retrieval, run SQL queries to our analytics store, and hit an internal graph tool. ideally stable function-calling (not flaky).
[02:08] Tom: from infra side we need V P C connectivity, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), audit logs, and SOC 2 evidence. also data residency config for EMEA.
[02:22] Samir: totally standard. Redwood Private supports on-prem/V P C with customer KMS; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and audit hooks; hosted is fastest to start.
[02:33] Aisha: quick question on quantization — are you recommending 4-bit quant for long context? i'm worried about hallucinations on domain terms.
[02:43] Priya: good question. quantization profiles are workload dependent. for retrieval-augmented tasks we usually keep higher precision for the head layers and experiment with mixed quantization. we can run evals on your prompt set to measure fidelity.
[02:55] Mark: can you support streaming responses with intermediate tool calls? e.g., stream token output while the assistant issues a retrieval tool call?
[03:06] Priya: yes — Redwood supports streaming and interleaved tool-calls, though the orchestration differs between hosted and dedicated. on dedicated we can reduce tail latency and customize batching.
[03:18] Tom: how about model variants — say we start with a smaller 8B model for prototyping then move to a 70B long-context variant — is that seamless?
[03:29] Samir: yes, same API across deployments. we can pin model versions and route by policy. fallback strategies are available if a high-accuracy variant hits capacity.
[03:40] Aisha: multilingual eval — do you have existing evals for spanish and japanese or do we need to provide?
[03:47] Priya: we have language-specific benchmarks but because of domain terminology your dataset will be most useful. please share sample prompts and reference outputs.
[03:56] Mark: we'll share sample prompts — about 200 prompts across languages plus a 30k token doc set for the long-context runs.
[04:06] Samir: perfect. rough sizing question — what's your expected concurrent sessions and tokens per second?
[04:13] Mark: expecting ~40 concurrent interactive sessions at peak, each may generate up to 200 tokens per response, plus background batch jobs. so capacity planning is key.
[04:25] Priya: that helps. for 40 concurrent with low-latency targets we'd recommend either Dedicated with a reserved pool sized for peak or Hosted with autoscaling but that can be more variable cost-wise.
[04:38] Tom: security — do you provide SSO/SAML for user console and RBAC? we need enterprise SSO and audit trails.
[04:46] Samir: yes SSO/SAML, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs are supported. for Private we can integrate with your IdP directly.
[04:54] Aisha: any limitations with function-calling for multiple simultaneous tool calls? like nesting calls or callback patterns?
[05:02] Priya: function-calling supports multiple tool invocations; nested orchestration is possible but we recommend a small orchestration layer in your app to keep state consistent. some edge cases show transient failures which we handle with idempotent retries.
[05:18] Mark: curious about cost — can you ballpark per-1M tokens hosted vs dedicated? rough numbers are fine.
[05:27] Samir: ballpark — hosted with a mid-size long-context model might be $X per 1M tokens; dedicated reduces unit cost by ~40% depending on utilization and quantization. i'll send exact pricing for expected usage.
[05:40] Tom: that delta is important; we need to justify dedicated commit to exec team.
[05:46] Aisha: benchmarks — can Redwood run a dedicated-run benchmark on our sample set? we'd like latency p50/p95 and token cost numbers.
[05:55] Priya: yes. if you provide the prompt/doc set and a target model list we'll run the bench on Dedicated and share results. for huge contexts we may need config tweaks (kv cache strategies).
[06:08] Mark: when you say kv cache strategies, can you explain? sometimes we've seen memory blow-up with naive caching.
[06:16] Priya: sure — we refer to KV cache for attention keys/values; we support prefix caching and chunked attention for long sequences to manage GPU memory. on dedicated we can tune chunk size and kernel selection. sometimes the tooling calls it k v cache or kvcache in logs — sorry, transcription idiosyncrasy.
[06:34] Samir: no worries. on the compliance front, i'll attach SOC 2 and ISO summary docs — and a note about our audit log retention options.
[06:42] Tom: for KMS, do you support HSM-backed keys? we need FIPS-level assurances.
[06:48] Samir: yes, HSM-backed KMS integrations are supported on Private and Dedicated via your cloud KMS or an HSM provider.
[06:56] Aisha: tool-calling reliability — any well-known gotchas? we've seen models change responses after quantization.
[07:04] Priya: yes, quantization can affect deterministic behavior. we'll include a regression test in the eval harness tied to your prompt set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles that keep key behaviors intact.
[07:18] Mark: timeline question — we want a pilot in Q3, ideally starting late july. is that feasible?
[07:25] Samir: yes, if we get prompts this week we can scope a two-week pilot on Dedicated starting late July.
[07:33] Tom: who from your side would run the benchmark?
[07:36] Priya: i'll run the benchmark and instrument the traces; samir will handle pricing and contracts.
[07:42] Aisha: when running the bench, can you include multilingual tokenization effects? spanish/japanese tokenization changes token counts.
[07:51] Priya: absolutely, we'll report tokenization per-language and effective token costs.
[07:58] Mark: do you support region pinning? our EMEA data has residency requirements.
[08:04] Samir: yes region pinning is available on Dedicated and Private. hosted has regional endpoints but Dedicated gives stronger guarantees.
[08:12] Tom: regarding network egress and V P C peering, any special requirements?
[08:18] Priya: we'll set up VPC peering or private endpoints; for on-prem we offer a Private control plane option.
[08:24] Mark: what about model lifecycle — how easy to roll a new model version or rollback if a regression appears?
[08:31] Samir: Redwood Console supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. you can pin model versions per route.
[08:40] Aisha: do you capture token-level cost/latency breakdowns for each route?
[08:45] Priya: yes, per-route dashboards with token/latency breakdowns and tracing hooks. helps root-cause regressions during rollouts.
[08:55] Mark: any notable limitations for 80k tokens?
[08:59] Priya: 80k is challenging — requires chunked attention and custom kernel selection; we can support it but you'll need Dedicated or Private with tuned configs. streaming behavior for that size will need careful UX design.
[09:12] Tom: last thing on security — SOC 2 report fine, but we also need to ensure data deletion on contract end.
[09:20] Samir: we support retention policies and on-termination data purge processes; documented in the security pack i'll send.
[09:28] Mark: ok great. let's talk about next steps — i'll summarize onshore end: we send prompts and doc set, internal stakeholders list, and target SLA.
[09:37] Samir: perfect. i'll send pricing and SOC docs; priya will schedule the tech deep dive / bench.
[09:44] Aisha: one more — do you support function-calling with typed schemas / OpenAPI-style contract?
[09:50] Priya: yes we support typed function-calls and schema enforcement; we can map to your internal API gateway patterns.
[09:57] Tom: fine. any competitor concerns we should be aware of? we've evaluated Anthropic and Mistral for long-context.
[10:05] Samir: common comparison points are latency, cost per token, and enterprise features. we'll include benchmark comparisons where relevant.
[10:13] Mark: ok good.

[10:20] (background cross-talk, notes exchanged)

[11:02] Samir: recap of owners and next steps — sending now: pricing, SOC docs, schedule deep-dive on 2027-07-22, and we'll start bench after Aisha shares prompts.
[11:20] Mark: sounds good. thanks all.
[11:24] Aisha: thanks.
[11:26] Tom: thanks.
